question.text: An investor submits a purchase application for Rs. 3,00,000 in an equity scheme at 2:30 PM on a business day. Funds are available for utilisation before the 3:00 PM cut-off on the same business day. The NAV on that day is Rs. 45.00 and the next day's NAV is Rs. 46.00. What NAV will be applicable and how many units will be allotted?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series V-A workbook (pp.190, 192), for equity/debt scheme purchases and switch-ins, the applicable NAV is the closing NAV of the day on which funds are available for utilisation before the 3:00 PM cut-off, irrespective of the time of receipt of the application and irrespective of the investment amount. Funds are stated to be available before 3:00 PM on the same business day, so same-day NAV of Rs. 45.00 applies. Units = Rs. 3,00,000 / Rs. 45.00 = 6,666.67 units. The Trap: Rs. 46.00 (next day's NAV) would apply only if funds were realised after 3:00 PM. Option C uses the right NAV but divides by the wrong number, and option D pairs the wrong NAV with the same-day unit count. Note that the pre-2021 "Rs. 2 lakh or more" framing has been superseded — funds-availability before cut-off is the single applicable rule today. Note: For NAV-sensitive purchases, recommend RTGS/NEFT/local cheques that achieve same-day fund credit. Outstation cheques or DDs that clear later push the applicable NAV to the day of actual fund availability.
